planning_notes: Preserve wiring from the supplied circuit: btn1 to Mega D2, servo1 PWM to Mega D3, servo2 PWM to Mega D4.

Debouncing and the press-to-toggle state machine (servo1: 0°->180°, servo2: 180°->0° and back) are implemented in the SysML model using elapsed_ms and the digital_input 'btn1 press command' model signal.
Both servos are initialized to 0° at startup as required.
Servo movement smoothness (ramp/slew) is handled in SysML; the interface requests only define the commanded angle ports.

Button active level is not specified in the circuit prose; treat the digital_input model value as true when the button is electrically HIGH per catalog default (active_high). If the actual pushbutton wiring is opposite, adjust active_high in the model logic rather than inverting the port model value here.

interfaces.meaning: Button btn1 press command (debounced in SysML)

interfaces.name: io_1
interfaces.meaning: servo1 angle command (toggles between 0° and 180° on each debounced press)

interfaces.name: io_2
interfaces.meaning: servo2 angle command (toggles between 0° and 180° on each debounced press)

configuration_resolution.original_requirement:
Target board is Arduino Mega 2560 as specified in the supplied circuit; use this board when the prose says UNO.


**Task**:
You are tasked with programming an Arduino (uno) to control two servo motors (servo1, servo2) using a push button (btn1). The servos should alternate their positions between 0° and 180° each time the button is pressed. Specifically, when the button is pressed, servo1 should move to 180° and servo2 should move to 0°, and vice versa on the next press.

**Detail Rules**:
Initialization: Upon powering on or resetting, both servos (servo1, servo2) should be set to 0°.
Button Interaction: Each press of the button (btn1) should toggle the positions of the servos. If servo1 is at 0° and servo2 is at 180°, pressing the button should move servo1 to 180° and servo2 to 0°. The next press should reverse their positions again.
Debouncing: The button press should be debounced to avoid false triggers caused by mechanical vibrations.
Servo Movement: The servos should move smoothly to their new positions after each button press.
